subject: OptiShield deployment: isolation options, SOC 2 status & next steps
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@optishield.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@optishield.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — items from this morning's call (isolation & compliance)

Tessa — thanks for the helpful conversation earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can prioritize internally: 

- Compliance posture: OptiShield is on track for SOC 2 Type II (in progress, auditor: ClearGate; expected audit completion Q4). We are also tracking GDPR implications for EEA users and have an internal DPA that we can share. HIPAA scope is under review for one product line; likely out of scope initially.
- Deployment preference: we’re leaning private VPC in our AWS account for Prod, with a strict ingress/egress policy. For an initial POC we’d consider a dedicated hosted instance.
- Isolation needs: we require network segmentation (no public IPs on model servers), optional air-gapped read-only sync for the most sensitive datasets, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.

Action items we need from Redwood:
1) A short diagram or reference topology showing the Private deployment (VPC peering vs. Transit Gateway) + recommended firewall rules.
2) A completed vendor security questionnaire (attached v1) — we’d like Redwood’s answers in a week.
3) Confirmation of SOC 2 status / evidence you can provide (ISO-style docs, auditor contact, or SOC 2 report).
4) Any constraints for air-gapped / offline sync options and what the operational cadence looks like.

We attached our questionnaire and a quick sketch of the network we had in mind. Can you confirm who on your side will own the questionnaire and circuit the diagram?

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
Head of IT Security, OptiShield
elena.park@optishield.com

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — items from this morning's call (isolation & compliance)

Elena — great to meet you earlier. High-level answers here and next steps below. I’ll loop in Rishi (solutions) and Monica (security ops) to own the questionnaire and the diagram respectively.

Short answers: 
- SOC 2: Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II (report issued 2026-05). We can share an NDA-gated copy and a short evidence pack (control owner list, encryption-at-rest/in-transit measures) once the legal team signs the confidentiality addendum.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We are GDPR-ready for data processing agreements and data subject request processes; HIPAA is supported via BAA for customers that require it — we can start BAA conversations if OptiShield expects PHI.
- Private deployment: We support VPC peering and Transit Gateway; our recommended pattern for strict isolation is Private deployment with no public IPs on inference nodes + NATed egress through controlled endpoints. Air-gapped sync is possible via periodic signed artifact transfer; we’ll outline operational constraints below.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Monica to complete the vendor questionnaire (target: 2026-09-06).
2) Rishi to draft a Private-deploy topology PDF + firewall rule template (target: 2026-09-03).
3) Tessa to share NDA/Confidentiality addendum link so we can exchange SOC 2 (today).
4) Sync call to walk the answers and diagram (30 min) — propose 2026-09-07 or 2026-09-08.

If that works, I’ll send calendar invites.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[tel] 415-555-0129

Subject: Re: Thanks — items from this morning's call (isolation & compliance)

Looping in with ownership on the questionnaire and a few technical clarifications for the diagram. Monica — I’ll hand you the file and my draft answers; can you validate the infra/security controls?

Notes for the questionnaire: 
- KMS: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS. For customer-managed keys we require a short onboarding window to set grant/policy.
- Network: For true zero-public IP we recommend Private deployment + VPC endpoints for control plane traffic. Transit Gateway works best at scale; VPC peering is simpler for single-account POCs.
- Air-gap: Our recommended pattern for air-gapped ingestion is an inbound-only S3 transfer job (signed manifest), executed by an ops-runner in a controlled subnet; this requires occasional manual verification and a maintenance window. We should call out RTO/RPO expectations in the questionnaire answers.

I’ll start filling out the spreadsheet and share a first pass by 2026-09-03.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena / Tom — thanks for the clear list and the attachments. I pulled the attached questionnaire into our tracker and started completing sections. A couple of things for OptiShield to confirm so our responses are precise: 

1) Which environment(s) do you want covered by the questionnaire responses? (POC only? POC + Prod?)
2) Do you need a BAA now or only if PHI is introduced later? If later, we’ll note the steps to initiate a BAA.
3) For the air-gapped workflow: can you confirm acceptable cadence (daily vs weekly) and whether OptiShield prefers an inbound-only transfer or a physically isolated transfer process?

What we will provide in the next delivery: 
- Completed vendor questionnaire (redlined where we need clarifications) — target: 2026-09-06.
- Private deployment reference diagram PDF with two options: VPC peering (POC) + Transit Gateway (scale) — target: 2026-09-03.
- NDA / SOC 2 exchange instructions (I’ll send the link to the confidentiality addendum and expected timeline for delivery of SOC 2 materials).

I’ll attach the first-pass answers to the tracker and flag items needing OptiShield confirmation. Sean — I’ve cc’d you for awareness of any escalation on timelines or executive sync.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Program Manager, Redwood Inference
